summary: Mount Hood NF ridge site: a 1925 tent, a 1933 L-4 cab, deactivated 1964 and burned 1967. A panel and remnants are described on site, and hikers visit.

facts.design: 1925 tent with firefinder and telephone; 1933 L-4 cab on the ridge below the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest
facts.status_note: The cab was burned in 1967; a trail guide describes remnants of the old lookout

access.note: Reached on foot from a trailhead parking area; a trail guide says the road is closed to motor vehicles August 15 to November 1

visit.trail_note: About a half-mile hike from the trailhead parking area (trail guide); the Oregon Hikers guide lists hikes of 1.2 to 13 miles that reach the site

events.note: Forest Service tent with firefinder and telephone erected (register); firelookout.com lists 1925 as a camp
Newspaper item says a new standard cabin had been built; the register and firelookout.com date the L-4 cab to 1933
L-4 cab built on the south end of the ridge below the summit
Staffed 74 days; reports by telephone to Dufur Ranger Station
Members of the Trails Club of Oregon staffed the station (called an AWS station)
Structure ignited by a Forest Service employee as the chosen method of disposal (November 1967)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1925 date is a tent and telephone camp, and the 1933 date is the L-4 cab. The two dates describe different things, so they do not conflict.

notes_for_editor: County is unresolved: the register says Wasco County, while firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page say Hood River County. The record's county is Wasco. The cabin date is unresolved: a 1932 newspaper item says a standard cabin was already built, while the register and firelookout.com give 1933. Burned 1967 (Forest Lookouts) and removed in the 1960s (trail guide) are not fully reconciled. The Oregon Hikers guide labels its hikes to the site 'Closed' without explaining why, so check current closures before a visit. The Trails Offroad road closure dates come from a paywalled guide excerpt and should be verified with the Forest Service. Access level 'public' rests on hiking guides; no Forest Service page was read.
